frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Checking at a closed boundary: an edge or surface that arrests crossing, so that what is on one side is held from passing to the other — verbally as stopping an advancing force at the line (with ʿan marking the shielded party), nominally as the palm, the body's own stopping-and-holding surface, and in kāffah as a collective whose boundary is sealed shut (no member outside it, none detaching from it).

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: Checking at a closed boundary: an edge or surface that arrests crossing, so that what is on one side is held from passing to the other — verbally as stopping an advancing force at the line (with ʿan marking the shielded party), nominally as the palm, the body's own stopping-and-holding surface, and in kāffah as a collective whose boundary is sealed shut (no member outside it, none detaching from it).
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root k-f-f is about a stopping edge. Eight verbal occurrences all describe halting something at a boundary so it cannot reach the other side: God restrains people's hands from the believers (48:20, 48:24, 5:11), restrains the Children of Israel from Jesus (5:110), may restrain the might of the disbelievers (4:84); believers are told to hold back their hands (4:77), hypocrites must withhold theirs (4:91); the disbelievers will be unable to hold the Fire back from their faces (21:39). The two noun occurrences name the palm (kaffayhi, 13:14 and 18:42) — the hand's flat checking-and-holding surface — both in scenes where it fails to retain anything (water that never reaches the mouth, wealth already lost). The five kāffah occurrences (2:208, 34:28, 9:122, 9:36 twice) describe a totality as a closed enclosure: enter peace with all of yourselves inside (2:208), fight and be fought as one unbroken body (9:36), do not march out as an undivided whole (9:122, where kāffah is explicitly opposed to a detached faction), and a mission whose reach closes around all people (34:28). One idea — a boundary that lets nothing cross — runs through restraining, the palm, and totality.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: the Form I verb contributes the transitive event 'cause X to stop'; the intensive feminine -ah in kāffah substantivizes the checking into a characterizing whole. CONSTRUCTION: the ʿan-phrase (present in all 8 verbal tokens) contributes the shielded party, not the root; the dual kaffayhi contributes body-part pairing; the accusative ḥāl position of kāffah contributes adverbial manner ('as/while being...'). CONTEXT: warfare and aggression supply the advancing hands/force in Cluster A; loss and futility supply the empty-palm pathos in Cluster B; communal address supplies the collective in Cluster C. After subtracting all of these, the non-empty residue is the closed checking edge itself — the surface at which crossing stops.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The kāffah cluster, sharpest at 2:208 'udkhulū fī s-silmi kāffatan' — 'enter into peace kāffah' reads on the surface as plain 'entirely/all together,' with no visible act of restraint, and could be claimed as a lexicalized adverb detached from the root. Resolution from inside the corpus: 9:122 opposes kāffah to a firqah/ṭāʾifah that separates out, and 2:208 immediately opposes it to following Satan's khuṭuwāt (step-by-step leakage out of the whole) — kāffah is totality construed as a sealed boundary, every member held within, which is the same checking-edge residue. The reconciliation works but requires this construal step, which is what caps the result at MODERATE.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Homonymy: two (or three) unrelated lexemes sharing the shape k-f-f — (a) kaff 'palm' as a primitive body-part noun, (b) kaffa 'restrain' as an independent verb, (c) kāffah as a frozen adverb 'entirely.' Under this hypothesis no single residue exists and the packet decomposes into three accidental clusters. The internal evidence against it: both palm occurrences are staged precisely as failed holding (13:14's palms that cannot bring water to the mouth), tying the noun to the holding function rather than mere anatomy; and kāffah is twice contextually opposed to partition/leakage (9:122, 2:208), tying it to closure rather than bare quantity. The unified reading explains these co-patternings; homonymy leaves them as coincidence.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors and contrasts: m-n-ʿ (prevent/withhold) denies access or grant without profiling any contact edge; ṣ-d-d (repel/turn away) deflects motion onto another path; ḥ-b-s (confine) and m-s-k (grasp/retain) profile keeping-in rather than stopping-at; r-d-d (turn back) reverses motion. k-f-f is distinctive in profiling the checking surface/edge itself at the moment of contact — which is why this root alone yields both the anatomical boundary-surface noun (kaff, palm) and the sealed-totality adverb (kāffah), outputs none of the neighboring roots produce. Falsifiable: a confirmed occurrence where k-f-f meant unbounded release, or where kāffah tolerated an explicit exception clause, would break the claim.
internal_discovery.rationale: All 15 confirmed occurrences were individually assessed and all 15 are reconcilable with a single residue: the closed checking boundary. The verbal cluster (8/8) exhibits it directly in a near-invariant construction (kaffa + force + ʿan + shielded party); the dual-noun cluster (2/2) names the body's checking-and-holding surface, both times in failed-retention scenes that presuppose the function; the kāffah cluster (5/5) instantiates it as sealed collective totality, supported internally by the kāffah-vs-ṭāʾifah opposition in 9:122 and the kāffah-vs-khuṭuwāt opposition in 2:208. Universal presence holds with zero inconsistent occurrences, so the result is PREFERRED. Strength is MODERATE rather than STRONG because (a) the kāffah cluster's link to the residue depends on a construal (totality-as-enclosure) rather than surface-transparent restraint, and (b) 34:28 kāffatan lil-nās is syntactically ambiguous between 'encompassing all people' and 'a checker of people' — though both readings carry the residue, so it does not threaten presence, only the sharpness of the demonstration.

adversarial_verification.notes: Full coverage checked: 15/15 accounted for (8 verbal Form I; 5 kāffah; 2 palm). VERBAL (21:39, 48:20, 48:24, 5:11, 5:110, 4:84, 4:77, 4:91): the residue "arrest an advancing force at the line, holding it from crossing to a shielded party" is demonstrably present in all eight; the ʿan-construction marking the shielded party appears in 21:39/48:20/48:24/5:11/5:110 and is implicit in the others. Strong, distinctive fit. KĀFFAH (2:208, 34:28, 9:122, 9:36 x2): standard sense "all together / whole"; the proposed "sealed collective, none detaching" is a defensible reframe of the group-held-together etymology — compatible, no refutation. FAILING occurrences = the two nominal palm cases. 13:14 (كَبَٰسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى ٱلْمَآءِ): the palms are SPREAD OPEN toward water and the water never reaches the mouth — the verse thematizes failure to hold/retain, the opposite of "a surface that arrests crossing / holds from passing"; the claimed arresting-boundary residue is not demonstrably present. 18:42 (يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ): palms TURNED OVER in a gesture of regret — pure body-part reference with no boundary/holding function active. The proposal over-specifies by importing the verbal "arrest at a closed boundary" semantics into the noun; the palm's actual salient sense is grasping/cupping (overlapping msk/qbD), and in these two occurrences even that holding is absent. Under non-negotiable root unity, two unreconciled confirmed occurrences bar SUPPORTED. Distinctiveness_ok=true for the verbal ward-off pattern (ʿan + shielded party is characteristic vs mnʿ/Hbs/msk), though the "surface/boundary" gloss blurs it at the palm. Falsifiable=true (predicts arrest-of-crossing present everywhere; the palm cases falsify the strong wording). Honest verdict: contribution holds for 13/15 but is not universally present as worded — PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED. Packet: D:\APP\tafseer\lisanapp3\data\campaign\packets\batch04\kff.json
